claims.claim: Lhx3 and Lhx4 antagonize Pax6-induced activation of the α-enhancer.
claims.source: In contrast, Lhx3 and Lhx4 do not affect α-enhancer activity alone (Figure 2A), but they antagonize Pax6-induced activation of the α-enhancer (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Isl1 is expressed in ON bipolar cells and cholinergic amacrine cells.
claims.source: Isl1 is expressed in ON bipolar cells and cholinergic amacrine cells (Elshatory et al., 2007; Galli-Resta et al., 1997; Haverkamp et al., 2003), but not in Pax6 α-enhancer-active amacrine cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Elshatory et al., 2007; Galli-Resta et al., 1997; Haverkamp et al., 2003) and immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B.

claims.claim: Isl1 is not expressed in Pax6 α-enhancer-active amacrine cells.
claims.source: Isl1 is expressed in ON bipolar cells and cholinergic amacrine cells (Elshatory et al., 2007; Galli-Resta et al., 1997; Haverkamp et al., 2003), but not in Pax6 α-enhancer-active amacrine cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B.

claims.claim: Isl1 does not affect Pax6 α-enhancer activity alone.
claims.source: Isl1 does not affect Pax6 α-enhancer activity alone, but it does activate the enhancer in the presence of Pax6 (Figure 2A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Isl1 activates the Pax6 α-enhancer in the presence of Pax6.
claims.source: Isl1 does not affect Pax6 α-enhancer activity alone, but it does activate the enhancer in the presence of Pax6 (Figure 2A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: LIM domain transcription factors in the mouse retina can be categorized as stimulatory (Lhx2 and Lhx9), inhibitory (Lhx3 and Lhx4), or context-sensitive (Isl1) based on their effects on Pax6 α-enhancer.
claims.source: Together, these results suggest LIM domain transcription factors in the mouse retina can be categorized based on how they affect Pax6 α-enhancer—some are stimulatory (i.e., Lhx2 and Lhx9), some are inhibitory (i.e., Lhx3 and Lhx4), and some are context-sensitive (i.e., Isl1).
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2A and 2B.

claims.claim: Tgfb1i1 inhibits Pax6-induced α-enhancer activity upon overexpression.
claims.source: Tgfb1i1, although it is unable to bind the α-enhancer directly (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B), inhibits Pax6-induced α-enhancer activity upon overexpression (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: The inhibition of the α-enhancer by Tgfb1i1 is more significant when Tgfb1i1 is co-expressed with both Lhx3 and Isl1.
claims.source: This inhibition of the α-enhancer is even more significant when Tgfb1i1 is co-expressed with both Lhx3 and Isl1 (Figure 2D,E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2D and 2E.

claims.claim: Multiple LIM domains of Tgfb1i1 allow it to form a multi-protein complex that blocks α-enhancer-dependent gene expression.
claims.source: We hypothesized that multiple LIM domains of Tgfb1i1 allow it to form a multi-protein complex that blocks α-enhancer-dependent gene expression.
claims.evidence: The claim is a hypothesis based on the known structure of Tgfb1i1 and the observed inhibitory effects on the α-enhancer.

claims.claim: Lmo4 prevents Isl1 and Lhx3 from interacting with one another or with other LIM domain-containing proteins.
claims.source: To assess this, we co-expressed these LIM domain transcription factors with Lmo4 (LIM-domain-only 4), which prevents Isl1 and Lhx3 from interacting with one another or with other LIM domain-containing proteins (Thaler et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Thaler et al., 2002, which characterized the function of Lmo4.

claims.claim: Lmo4 alone causes a dose-dependent increase in α-enhancer activity.
claims.source: Lmo4 alone caused a dose-dependent increase in α-enhancer activity and potentiated Pax6-induced activation of the α-enhancer (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Lmo4 potentiates Pax6-induced activation of the α-enhancer.
claims.source: Lmo4 alone caused a dose-dependent increase in α-enhancer activity and potentiated Pax6-induced activation of the α-enhancer (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: In the presence of Lmo4, Lhx3 and Isl1 cannot inhibit the α-enhancer.
claims.source: In the presence of Lmo4, Lhx3 and Isl1 cannot inhibit the α-enhancer (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Tgfb1i1 and Lmo4 oppositely regulate α-enhancer activity by antagonistically modulating the formation of the LIM domain transcription factor complex.
claims.source: Thus, Tgfb1i1 and Lmo4 appear to oppositely regulate α-enhancer activity by antagonistically modulating the formation of the LIM domain transcription factor complex.
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective luciferase reporter assay data showing opposite effects of Tgfb1i1 and Lmo4.

claims.claim: Isl1 is detected in complexes recovered using Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 from P7 mouse retina.
claims.source: We were able to detect Isl1 in complexes recovered using Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1, which are also capable of precipitating one another (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 are capable of precipitating one another in P7 mouse retina.
claims.source: We were able to detect Isl1 in complexes recovered using Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1, which are also capable of precipitating one another (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Isl1, Lhx3, and Tgfb1i1 may exist as a complex in the retina.
claims.source: This suggests these three proteins may exist as a complex in the retina.
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the co-immunoprecipitation data showing mutual interactions among the three proteins.

claims.claim: Isl1 binds to Lhx3 with its homeodomain (HD) and/or LIM binding domain (LBD).
claims.source: In the co-immunoprecipitation experiments, we found that Isl1 binds to Lhx3 with its homeodomain (HD) and/or LIM binding domain (LBD), as reported previously (Thaler et al., 2002), whereas it interacts with Tgfb1i1 with its LIM domain(s) (Figure 3B [left column]; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C, and corroborated by citation to Thaler et al., 2002.

claims.claim: Isl1 interacts with Tgfb1i1 with its LIM domain(s).
claims.source: In the co-immunoprecipitation experiments, we found that Isl1 binds to Lhx3 with its homeodomain (HD) and/or LIM binding domain (LBD), as reported previously (Thaler et al., 2002), whereas it interacts with Tgfb1i1 with its LIM domain(s) (Figure 3B [left column]; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C.

claims.claim: Lhx3 binds to Tgfb1i1 and Isl1 via its LIM domain(s).
claims.source: Lhx3 binds to Tgfb1i1 and Isl1 via its LIM domain(s) (Figure 3B [center column]; Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F.

claims.claim: Tgfb1i1 uses LIM domain(s) to interact with Isl1 and Lhx3.
claims.source: Tgfb1i1 also uses LIM domain(s) to interact with Isl1 and Lhx3 (Figure 3B [right columns]; Figure 3—figure supplement 1H,I).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1H,I.

claims.claim: Overexpressed Tgfb1i1 enhances the association between Lhx3 and Isl1.
claims.source: We found overexpressed Tgfb1i1 further enhanced the association between Lhx3 and Isl1 (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Lmo4 induces a dose-dependent decrease in the association between Isl1 and Lhx3.
claims.source: Lmo4, in contrast, induces a dose-dependent decrease in the association between Isl1 and Lhx3 (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: Tgfb1i1 links Isl1 and Lhx3 to form a hetero-tetrameric (or larger) complex while Lmo4 interferes with the complex formation.
claims.source: Collectively, these results suggest Tgfb1i1 links Isl1 and Lhx3 to form a hetero-tetrameric (or larger) complex while Lmo4 interferes with the complex formation.
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective co-immunoprecipitation data showing Tgfb1i1 enhances and Lmo4 reduces Isl1-Lhx3 association.

claims.claim: Pax6 interacts with various homeodomain-containing proteins.
claims.source: It is possible Pax6 interacts with the homeodomains of Isl1 and Lhx3 to form a Pax6-LIM protein complex, since Pax6 reportedly interacts with various homeodomain-containing proteins (Granger et al., 2006; Mikkola et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Granger et al., 2006; Mikkola et al., 2001) that demonstrated Pax6 interactions with homeodomain proteins.

claims.claim: Pax6 interacts only with Isl1, but not Lhx3, via its paired domain (PD).
claims.source: We also found Pax6 interacts only with Isl1, but not Lhx3, via its paired domain (PD) (Figure 3E; Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claims.claim: Both the HD and LIM domains of Isl1 participate in interaction with Pax6.
claims.source: Both the HD and LIM domains of Isl1 participated to interact with Pax6, thus Pax6 might compete with Tgfb1i1 and Lhx3 to bind Isl1 (Figure 3H, top; Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: Pax6 might compete with Tgfb1i1 and Lhx3 to bind Isl1.
claims.source: Both the HD and LIM domains of Isl1 participated to interact with Pax6, thus Pax6 might compete with Tgfb1i1 and Lhx3 to bind Isl1 (Figure 3H, top; Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that Pax6 and Tgfb1i1/Lhx3 bind overlapping domains of Isl1.

claims.claim: Isl1, Lhx3, and Tgfb1i1 reduce the binding of Pax6 to the α-enhancer when all three are co-expressed.
claims.source: Using ChIP analyses in the cultured cells, we found Isl1, Lhx3, and Tgfb1i1 reduce the binding of Pax6 to the α-enhancer when all three are co-expressed but not when expressed individually (Figure 3G, three right graphs).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 3G.

claims.claim: Pax6 expression interferes with the access of Tgfb1i1 to the α-enhancer.
claims.source: Conversely, Pax6 expression interferes with the access of Tgfb1i1 to the α-enhancer (Figure 3G, rightmost graph).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 3G.

claims.claim: Pax6 does not affect Lhx3 binding to the α-enhancer.
claims.source: Pax6 does not affect Lhx3 binding to the α-enhancer, but it promotes Isl1 binding (Figure 3H, two center graphs).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 3H.

claims.claim: Pax6 promotes Isl1 binding to the α-enhancer.
claims.source: Pax6 does not affect Lhx3 binding to the α-enhancer, but it promotes Isl1 binding (Figure 3H, two center graphs).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 3H.

claims.claim: Two different transcription factor complexes occupy the α-enhancer region: the Isl1-Pax6 complex that activates the α-enhancer, and the Isl1-Tgfb1i1-Lhx3 complex that inhibits Pax6 access.
claims.source: Together, these molecular interaction results suggest two different transcription factor complexes occupying the α-enhancer region. The Isl1-Pax6 complex binds to the DF3 and PBS and activates the α-enhancer (Figure 3H, top), whereas the Isl1-Tgfb1i1-Lhx3 complex binds to DF3 and DF4 to cover the area between those two sequences and inhibit the access of Pax6 to DF3 (Figure 3H, bottom).
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective ChIP and co-immunoprecipitation data, summarized in Figure 3H.

claims.claim: Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas show more cells positive for the Pax6 α-GFP reporter than the retinas of their Tgfb1i1+/+ littermates.
claims.source: In support of the idea that Tgfb1i1 plays an important role in the inhibition of Pax6 α-enhancer, the Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas show more cells positive for the Pax6 α-GFP reporter than the retinas of their Tgfb1i1+/+ littermates (Figure 4A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claims.claim: Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas have more Pax6-positive amacrine cells than Tgfb1i1+/+ littermates.
claims.source: Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas have more Pax6-positive amacrine cells and fewer Vsx2-positive bipolar cells than Tgfb1i1+/+ littermates (Figure 4C–F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4C-F.

claims.claim: Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas have fewer Vsx2-positive bipolar cells than Tgfb1i1+/+ littermates.
claims.source: Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas have more Pax6-positive amacrine cells and fewer Vsx2-positive bipolar cells than Tgfb1i1+/+ littermates (Figure 4C–F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4C-F.

claims.claim: Among amacrine cell subtypes, only GABAergic amacrine cells show a significant increase in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.
claims.source: Among those amacrine cell subtypes, only GABAergic amacrine cells showed a significant increase, while the numbers of cholinergic and glycinergic amacrine cells remain unchanged (Figure 4C,D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4C and 4D.

claims.claim: The numbers of cholinergic and glycinergic amacrine cells remain unchanged in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.
claims.source: Among those amacrine cell subtypes, only GABAergic amacrine cells showed a significant increase, while the numbers of cholinergic and glycinergic amacrine cells remain unchanged (Figure 4C,D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4C and 4D.

claims.claim: The Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells are mainly GABAergic amacrine cells.
claims.source: Moreover, the Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells are mainly GABAergic amacrine cells (Figure 4C,D; Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting a positive relationship between Pax6 α-enhancer activity and GABAergic amacrine cell fate and a negative role of Tgfb1i1 in this.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4C, 4D, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: There is a positive relationship between Pax6 α-enhancer activity and GABAergic amacrine cell fate.
claims.source: Moreover, the Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells are mainly GABAergic amacrine cells (Figure 4C,D; Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting a positive relationship between Pax6 α-enhancer activity and GABAergic amacrine cell fate and a negative role of Tgfb1i1 in this.
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells are predominantly GABAergic.

claims.claim: Tgfb1i1 plays a negative role in GABAergic amacrine cell fate.
claims.source: Moreover, the Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells are mainly GABAergic amacrine cells (Figure 4C,D; Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting a positive relationship between Pax6 α-enhancer activity and GABAergic amacrine cell fate and a negative role of Tgfb1i1 in this.
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the increase in GABAergic amacrine cells in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.

claims.claim: The Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas show fewer Vsx1-positive OFF bipolar cells without significant changes in G0α-positive ON bipolar cells.
claims.source: Among bipolar cell subtypes, the Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas show fewer Vsx1-positive OFF bipolar cells without significant changes in G0α-positive ON bipolar cells, including PKCα-positive rod bipolar cells (Figure 4E,F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4E and 4F.

claims.claim: The numbers of type-2 OFF bipolar cells, which are positive to Bhlhb5 and Recoverin, are not greatly different between Tgfb1i1+/+ and Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas.
claims.source: However, the numbers of type-2 OFF bipolar cells, which are positive to Bhlhb5 and Recoverin, are not greatly different between Tgfb1i1+/+ and Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas (Figure 4C–F; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 4C-F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Tgfb1i1 is necessary for the development of Vsx1-positive OFF bipolar cells, except for type-2 subset, in mouse retina.
claims.source: The results therefore suggest that Tgfb1i1 is necessary for the development of Vsx1-positive OFF bipolar cells, except for type-2 subset, in mouse retina.
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the selective reduction of Vsx1-positive OFF bipolar cells (excluding type-2) in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.

claims.claim: GABAergic amacrine cell identities of retinal cells expressing Cas9 and Lhx3 sgRNA were significantly enhanced.
claims.source: We found GABAergic amacrine cell identities of the retinal cells expressing the constructs were significantly enhanced, whereas OFF bipolar cell identities of the cells were remarkably diminished (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B–D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from CRISPR/Cas9-mediated Lhx3 deletion experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B-D.

claims.claim: OFF bipolar cell identities of retinal cells expressing Cas9 and Lhx3 sgRNA were remarkably diminished.
claims.source: We found GABAergic amacrine cell identities of the retinal cells expressing the constructs were significantly enhanced, whereas OFF bipolar cell identities of the cells were remarkably diminished (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B–D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from CRISPR/Cas9-mediated Lhx3 deletion experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B-D.

claims.claim: Tgfb1i1 supports the development of OFF bipolar cell subsets while it antagonizes the development of GABAergic amacrine cell subset by forming Lhx3-containing protein complex that inhibits Pax6 α-enhancer activity in post-natal mouse retina.
claims.source: Collectively, our results suggest that Tgfb1i1 supports the development of OFF bipolar cell subsets, while it antagonizes the development of GABAergic amacrine cell subset, by forming Lhx3-containing protein complex that inhibits Pax6 α-enhancer activity in post-natal mouse retina.
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the collective data from Tgfb1i1−/− and Lhx3 deletion experiments.

claims.claim: In P14 mouse retinas, Lhx3-positive bipolar cells co-expressing Isl1 comprise only 20% of total Lhx3-positive cells.
claims.source: In P14 mouse retinas, Lhx3-positive bipolar cells co-expressing Isl1 comprise only 20% of total Lhx3-positive cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and 1C.

claims.claim: 82% of Lhx3-positive retinal cells co-express Isl1 at P7.
claims.source: In contrast, 82% of Lhx3-positive retinal cells co-express Isl1 at P7, which is when Tgfb1i1 is expressed in most retinal cell types apart from amacrine cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and 1C.

claims.claim: The Isl1-Tgfb1i1-Lhx3 complex may form in the retinal cells around the first post-natal week at the peak of bipolar cell development.
claims.source: This suggests the Isl1-Tgfb1i1-Lhx3 complex may form in the retinal cells around the first post-natal week at the peak of bipolar cell development (Morrow et al., 2008; Rapaport et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the temporal expression patterns of the proteins, supported by citations to studies on bipolar cell development (Morrow et al., 2008; Rapaport et al., 2004).

claims.claim: The interaction between Isl1 and Lhx3 is significantly reduced in P7 Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.
claims.source: Supporting this, the interaction between Isl1 and Lhx3 is significantly reduced in P7 Tgfb1i1−/− retinas (Figure 5A, top).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: Reduced Isl1-Lhx3 interaction might trigger an over-activation of Pax6 transcription driven by the α-enhancer.
claims.source: This might trigger an over-activation of Pax6 transcription, driven by the α-enhancer.
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the reduced Isl1-Lhx3 interaction in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.

claims.claim: Pax6 levels did not differ in Tgfb1i1−/− and Tgfb1i1+/+ mouse retinas.
claims.source: However, Pax6 levels did not differ in Tgfb1i1−/− and Tgfb1i1+/+ mouse retinas (Figure 5B, larger Pax6 bands), despite the increase of Pax6-positive cells in Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retina (Figure 4C,D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: A specific increase in the level of Pax6ΔPD isoform was observed in the Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retina.
claims.source: We did, instead, observe a specific increase in the level of Pax6ΔPD isoform, which is an alternative transcript produced at downstream of the α-enhancer sequence (Lakowski et al., 2007; Plaza et al., 1995), in the Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retina (Figure 5B, smaller Pax6 bands).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B and citations to previous studies (Lakowski et al., 2007; Plaza et al., 1995) characterizing the Pax6ΔPD isoform.

claims.claim: Pax6ΔPD isoform is selectively enriched in Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells purified from P7 P6α-CreiGFP retinas by FACS.
claims.source: This Pax6ΔPD isoform is selectively enriched in Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells purified from P7 P6α-CreiGFP retinas by fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data from FACS-purified cells shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Hyperactivation of the Pax6 α-enhancer in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas triggers ectopic expression of Pax6ΔPD isoform, but not the canonical Pax6.
claims.source: Our results, thus, suggest hyperactivation of the Pax6 α-enhancer in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas triggers ectopic expression of Pax6ΔPD isoform, but not the canonical Pax6.
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the selective increase in Pax6ΔPD but not full-length Pax6 in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.

claims.claim: About 54% of EGFP-positive INL cells in P14 mouse retinas electroporated with pCAGIG-Pax6ΔPD DNA at P0 are identified as Syntaxin-positive amacrine cells.
claims.source: About 54% of EGFP-positive INL cells in P14 mouse retinas, which were electroporated with the pCAGIG-Pax6ΔPD DNA at P0, are identified as Syntaxin-positive amacrine cells, whereas only 26% of EGFP-positive INL cells are amacrine cells in the retinas electroporated with control pCAGIG DNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A [top row], D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from electroporation experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and 2D.

claims.claim: About 85% of EGFP-positive INL cells in P14 mouse retinas electroporated with pCAGIG-Pax6 DNA at P0 are identified as amacrine cells.
claims.source: This is also contrary to the results of pCAGIG-Pax6-electroporated mouse retinas, in which about 85% of EGFP-positive INL cells are identified as amacrine cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A [top row, middle], D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from electroporation experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and 2D.

claims.claim: Majority of EGFP-positive amacrine cells in the pCAGIG-Pax6ΔPD-electroporated retinas are predicted as GABAergic amacrine cells.
claims.source: Moreover, by showing insignificantly different marker positivity with EGFP;Syntaxin double-positive INL cells (54% ± 7.56%(Syntaxin) vs. 46% ± 7.33%(Gad67)), majority of EGFP-positive amacrine cells in the pCAGIG-Pax6ΔPD-electroporated retinas are predicted as GABAergic amacrine cells, which are approximately half of the EGFP;Syntaxin double-positive amacrine cell population in pCAGIG-Pax6-electroporated mouse retinas (85% ± 7.2%(Syntaxin) vs. 44% ± 9.17%(Gad67)) (Figure 5F,G; Figure 5—figure supplement 2A [second row], D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from electroporation experiments shown in Figure 5F, 5G, and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and 2D.

claims.claim: Pax6ΔPD preferentially supports GABAergic amacrine cell fate.
claims.source: Together, these results suggest that Pax6ΔPD preferentially supports GABAergic amacrine cell fate, while full-length Pax6 induces all amacrine cell types in a similar ratio observed in the normal mouse retina (Voinescu et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the electroporation data showing preferential GABAergic fate in Pax6ΔPD-expressing cells, with citation to Voinescu et al., 2009 for normal amacrine cell ratios.

claims.claim: Full-length Pax6 induces all amacrine cell types in a similar ratio observed in the normal mouse retina.
claims.source: Together, these results suggest that Pax6ΔPD preferentially supports GABAergic amacrine cell fate, while full-length Pax6 induces all amacrine cell types in a similar ratio observed in the normal mouse retina (Voinescu et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the electroporation data, with citation to Voinescu et al., 2009 for normal amacrine cell ratios.

claims.claim: Mouse retinas expressing ectopic Pax6ΔPD show almost no EGFP-positive cells co-expressing OFF bipolar cell markers including Vsx1, Recoverin, and Bhlhb5.
claims.source: Mouse retinas expressing ectopic Pax6ΔPD show almost no EGFP-positive cells co-expressing OFF bipolar cell markers including Vsx1, Recoverin, and Bhlhb5 (Figure 5F [bottom row], G; Figure 5—figure supplement 2B,D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from electroporation experiments shown in Figure 5F, 5G, and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and 2D.

claims.claim: Significant numbers of EGFP-positive cells co-expressed ON bipolar cell marker G0α in pCAGIG-Pax6ΔPD-electroporated mouse retinas.
claims.source: On the contrary, significant numbers of EGFP-positive cells co-expressed ON bipolar cell marker G0α in pCAGIG-Pax6ΔPD-electroporated mouse retinas, and the numbers are not significantly different from those in pCAGIG-electroporated samples (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B,D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from electroporation experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and 2D.

claims.claim: EGFP-positive cells in pCAGIG-Pax6-electroporated mouse retinas are almost absent of both ON and OFF bipolar cell marker co-expression.
claims.source: EGFP-positive cells in pCAGIG-Pax6-electroporated mouse retinas, however, are almost absent of both ON and OFF bipolar cell marker co-expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B,D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data from electroporation experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and 2D.

claims.claim: Pax6ΔPD inhibits only OFF bipolar cell fate.
claims.source: The results therefore suggest that Pax6ΔPD inhibits only OFF bipolar cell fate, while full-length Pax6 suppress both ON and OFF bipolar cell fates.
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference based on the electroporation data showing selective loss of OFF bipolar markers in Pax6ΔPD-expressing cells.

claims.claim: Full-length Pax6 suppresses both ON and OFF bipolar cell fates.
claims.source: The results therefore suggest that Pax6ΔPD inhibits only OFF bipolar cell fate, while full-length Pax6 suppress both ON and OFF bipolar cell fates.

results.result: Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 were identified as DF4-binding proteins through proteomic screening in R28 rat retinal precursor cells. Validation experiments confirmed that Lhx3 directly binds DF4 DNA through its homeodomain, while Tgfb1i1 lacks DNA-binding motifs and associates with the α-enhancer indirectly. ChIP analysis demonstrated that both proteins specifically interact with the α-enhancer but not the ectodermal enhancer in mouse retina.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C12-C16 provide converging evidence from proteomic screening (C1), DNA pull-down assays (C12), EMSA with in vitro translated proteins (C13-C14), and in vivo ChIP (C16). The data consistently show Lhx3 directly binds DF4 while Tgfb1i1 associates indirectly, with appropriate controls (mutant DF4 sequences) demonstrating specificity.

results.result: Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 share the LIM protein-protein interaction domain. Lhx3 additionally contains a homeodomain and functions as a transcription factor, while Tgfb1i1 has four leucine-rich domains and four LIM domains that mediate protein-protein interactions and self-oligomerization.
results.evaluation: Claims C2-C5 are supported by citations to established literature characterizing these protein domains and their functions. These are well-established structural features of these proteins based on prior work (Karlsson et al., 1990; Way and Chalfie, 1988; Bridwell et al., 2001; Roberson et al., 1994; Mori et al., 2006; Nishiya et al., 1999).

results.result: Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 show distinct temporal expression patterns in mouse retina. Lhx3 is absent from embryonic retina but expressed in bipolar cells beginning around the first postnatal week. Tgfb1i1 is expressed in most of postnatal retina but absent from embryonic and adult retinas. Cells expressing Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 in P8 retinas show no Pax6 α-enhancer activity, suggesting a negative relationship.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C11 are supported by immunostaining data in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B, corroborated by citation to Balasubramanian et al., 2014. The temporal expression patterns are clearly documented, and the lack of co-localization with Pax6 α-GFP reporter provides evidence for the proposed negative relationship (C11).

results.result: Different LIM domain transcription factors show distinct DNA-binding specificities within the Pax6 α-enhancer. Lhx2 binds DF4 sequence while Isl1 does not; conversely, Isl1 binds DF3 (containing the Isl1 consensus sequence 5'-CATTAG-3') while Lhx2 and Lhx3 do not. This suggests Tgfb1i1 binds the α-enhancer indirectly through interactions with LIM domain transcription factors.
results.evaluation: Claims C17-C21 are supported by EMSA data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C-D showing differential binding specificities. The binding of Isl1 to DF3 is consistent with its known consensus sequence (Lee et al., 2008; Leonard et al., 1992). The inference that Tgfb1i1 binds indirectly (C21) is logical given it lacks DNA-binding motifs but associates with the enhancer.

results.result: LIM domain transcription factors in mouse retina can be functionally categorized based on their effects on Pax6 α-enhancer activity. Lhx2 and Lhx9 are stimulatory, activating the α-luciferase reporter in a dose-dependent manner. Lhx3 and Lhx4 are inhibitory, antagonizing Pax6-induced activation without affecting basal activity. Isl1 is context-sensitive, activating the enhancer only in the presence of Pax6. These factors show distinct expression patterns in retinal cell types.
results.evaluation: Claims C22-C32 are supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 2A-B) and immunostaining data (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A-B) with appropriate citations. The functional categorization (C32) is a reasonable inference from the dose-response data. The cell-type expression patterns are corroborated by multiple sources including Balasubramanian et al., 2014.

results.result: Tgfb1i1 and Lmo4 oppositely regulate α-enhancer activity by antagonistically modulating LIM domain transcription factor complex formation. Tgfb1i1 inhibits Pax6-induced α-enhancer activity, with enhanced inhibition when co-expressed with Lhx3 and Isl1. Lmo4 causes dose-dependent increases in α-enhancer activity and prevents Lhx3/Isl1-mediated inhibition by interfering with protein-protein interactions.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C40 are supported by luciferase reporter assays in Figure 2C-E showing opposite effects of Tgfb1i1 and Lmo4. The mechanism involving Lmo4 interference with LIM protein interactions is supported by citation to Thaler et al., 2002. The hypothesis about Tgfb1i1 forming multi-protein complexes (C35) is reasonable given its multiple LIM domains, though speculative.

results.result: Isl1, Lhx3, and Tgfb1i1 form a protein complex in P7 mouse retina. Co-immunoprecipitation experiments demonstrate mutual interactions among these proteins, with specific domain requirements: Isl1 binds Lhx3 via HD/LBD and Tgfb1i1 via LIM domains; Lhx3 and Tgfb1i1 interact via their LIM domains. Tgfb1i1 enhances Isl1-Lhx3 association while Lmo4 reduces it, suggesting Tgfb1i1 links these proteins into a hetero-tetrameric or larger complex.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C50 are supported by co-immunoprecipitation data in Figure 3A-D and domain mapping experiments in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1. The reciprocal co-IPs demonstrate mutual interactions, and domain deletion experiments identify specific interaction interfaces. The opposing effects of Tgfb1i1 and Lmo4 on complex formation are clearly demonstrated.

results.result: Two distinct transcription factor complexes occupy the Pax6 α-enhancer region with opposing functions. The Isl1-Pax6 complex binds DF3 and PBS to activate the α-enhancer, with Pax6 interacting with Isl1 (but not Lhx3) via its paired domain. The Isl1-Tgfb1i1-Lhx3 complex binds DF3 and DF4, inhibiting Pax6 access to the enhancer. ChIP experiments show these complexes mutually interfere with each other's binding.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C59 are supported by co-immunoprecipitation data (Figure 3E, 3H) and ChIP experiments in cultured cells (Figure 3G). The domain mapping (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) confirms specific interaction interfaces. The model of two competing complexes (C59) is a reasonable inference from the mutual interference observed in ChIP experiments, though direct evidence of simultaneous binding competition in vivo would strengthen this conclusion.

results.result: Tgfb1i1−/− mouse retinas show increased Pax6 α-enhancer activity and altered retinal cell composition. These retinas have more Pax6 α-GFP reporter-positive cells and more Pax6-positive amacrine cells, with a specific increase in GABAergic amacrine cells while cholinergic and glycinergic populations remain unchanged. Conversely, Vsx2-positive bipolar cells are reduced. The Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells are predominantly GABAergic, suggesting Tgfb1i1 negatively regulates GABAergic amacrine cell fate.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C67 are supported by immunostaining and quantification data in Figure 4A-F. The cell counting is systematic with appropriate markers for different cell types. The statistical significance is indicated. The inference about Tgfb1i1's negative role (C67) is logical given the increased GABAergic cells in knockout mice, though the mechanism requires further validation.

results.result: Tgfb1i1 is necessary for development of specific OFF bipolar cell subsets. Tgfb1i1−/− retinas show fewer Vsx1-positive OFF bipolar cells without changes in ON bipolar cells, but type-2 OFF bipolar cells (Bhlhb5/Recoverin-positive) are unaffected. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of Lhx3 in postnatal retina enhances GABAergic amacrine cell identity while diminishing OFF bipolar cell identity, supporting the model that Tgfb1i1 forms Lhx3-containing complexes to support OFF bipolar development while antagonizing GABAergic amacrine fate.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C73 are supported by immunostaining data (Figure 4E-F) and CRISPR/Cas9 experiments (Figure 4—figure supplement 2). The selective effect on Vsx1-positive but not type-2 OFF bipolar cells is clearly documented. The Lhx3 deletion experiments provide functional validation, though the CRISPR approach may have incomplete penetrance or off-target effects that should be considered.

results.result: The Isl1-Tgfb1i1-Lhx3 complex forms transiently during the first postnatal week at the peak of bipolar cell development. At P7, 82% of Lhx3-positive cells co-express Isl1, compared to only 20% at P14. Supporting this temporal pattern, Isl1-Lhx3 interaction is significantly reduced in P7 Tgfb1i1−/− retinas, which might trigger over-activation of Pax6 transcription driven by the α-enhancer.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C78 are supported by immunostaining quantification (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) and co-immunoprecipitation data (Figure 5A). The temporal correlation with bipolar cell development is supported by citations (Morrow et al., 2008; Rapaport et al., 2004). The inference about Pax6 over-activation (C78) is logical but requires direct measurement of transcriptional activity.

results.result: Hyperactivation of the Pax6 α-enhancer in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas triggers selective ectopic expression of the Pax6ΔPD isoform rather than canonical Pax6. Western blot analysis shows no difference in full-length Pax6 levels between Tgfb1i1−/− and wild-type retinas, but a specific increase in Pax6ΔPD isoform. FACS-purified Pax6 α-GFP-positive cells are selectively enriched for Pax6ΔPD.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C82 are supported by Western blot data (Figure 5B-C) showing differential expression of Pax6 isoforms. The FACS purification (Figure 5C) provides strong evidence that Pax6ΔPD is specifically enriched in α-enhancer-active cells. The citations to Lakowski et al., 2007 and Plaza et al., 1995 support the characterization of Pax6ΔPD as an alternative transcript downstream of the α-enhancer.

results.result: Pax6ΔPD preferentially supports GABAergic amacrine cell fate while full-length Pax6 induces all amacrine cell types. Electroporation experiments show that Pax6ΔPD overexpression results in 54% of EGFP-positive INL cells being amacrine cells (predominantly GABAergic), compared to 85% for full-length Pax6 (which induces all amacrine subtypes in normal ratios). This differential activity explains the specific increase in GABAergic amacrine cells in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C87 are supported by electroporation experiments with quantification (Figure 5F-G, Figure 5—figure supplement 2). The data clearly show differential effects of Pax6 versus Pax6ΔPD on cell fate determination. The comparison to normal amacrine cell ratios is supported by citation to Voinescu et al., 2009. However, overexpression experiments may not fully recapitulate endogenous expression levels.

results.result: Pax6ΔPD selectively inhibits OFF bipolar cell fate while full-length Pax6 suppresses both ON and OFF bipolar cell fates. Electroporation of Pax6ΔPD shows almost no EGFP-positive cells co-expressing OFF bipolar markers (Vsx1, Recoverin, Bhlhb5) but significant numbers expressing ON bipolar marker G0α. In contrast, full-length Pax6 overexpression results in absence of both ON and OFF bipolar markers.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C92 are supported by electroporation data (Figure 5F, Figure 5—figure supplement 2B,D). The differential effects on bipolar cell subtypes are clearly documented with appropriate markers. The inferences about selective inhibition (C91-C92) are reasonable based on the marker expression patterns, though the mechanisms remain to be elucidated.

results.result: Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mice with deleted auto-stimulatory PBS in the α-enhancer show normal eye morphology but reduced α-enhancer activity. Despite normal gross eye development, P14 Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas show significantly reduced but not abolished α-enhancer-driven GFP and Pax6ΔPD expression. Since Pax6 cannot bind the mutant enhancer, this suggests the presence of other positive regulators of the α-enhancer in mouse retina.
results.evaluation: Claims C93-C96 are supported by eye morphology images (Figure 6B), immunostaining (Figure 6B-C), and Western blot data (Figure 6D). The CRISPR/Cas9-generated deletion is confirmed by sequencing (Figure 6A). The inference about additional positive regulators (C96) is supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 showing Pax6 cannot activate the ΔPBS enhancer, though the identity of these regulators remains unknown.

results.result: Pax6-dependent activation of the Pax6 α-enhancer is not essential for embryonic GABAergic amacrine cell development but is necessary for their postnatal maintenance. P14 Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas show fewer GABAergic amacrine cells and more OFF bipolar cells compared to wild-type, despite similar total amacrine and bipolar cell numbers. However, GABAergic amacrine cell numbers are normal until P4, suggesting the α-enhancer becomes important during postnatal development.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-C101 are supported by immunostaining and quantification data (Figure 6E-F, Figure 6—figure supplement 2-3). The temporal analysis (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A-B) clearly shows normal GABAergic cell numbers until P4, supporting the inference about postnatal-specific function (C100-C101). The citation to Voinescu et al., 2009 supports the timing of GABAergic amacrine cell development.

results.result: The altered OFF bipolar cell numbers in Tgfb1i1−/− and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas result from fate changes of preexisting cells rather than altered neurogenesis. BrdU labeling between P4-P7 shows no newborn GABAergic amacrine cells in any genotype, and the numbers of newly born OFF bipolar cells are similar across genotypes despite dramatic differences in total OFF bipolar cell numbers. This indicates postnatal transdifferentiation rather than altered cell fate specification during neurogenesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C105 are supported by BrdU labeling experiments (Figure 6—figure supplement 3C-E). The absence of BrdU-labeled GABAergic amacrine cells born postnatally (C102-C103) and unchanged numbers of newly born OFF bipolar cells (C104) provide strong evidence for the transdifferentiation model (C105). However, the possibility of cell death contributing to the phenotype is not fully addressed.

results.result: Pax6 and the Isl1-Tgfb1i1-Lhx3 complex competitively regulate Pax6 α-enhancer-driven Pax6ΔPD expression to maintain GABAergic amacrine cell fate against transdifferentiation into OFF bipolar cells. BrdU labeling from E15 shows that embryonically-born cells in Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas have significantly decreased GABAergic amacrine cell identity and increased OFF bipolar cell identity at P7, demonstrating fate conversion of cells born during the amacrine cell genesis period.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C108 are supported by BrdU labeling from E15 (Figure 6—figure supplement 3D,F) showing reciprocal changes in cell fate. The data demonstrate that cells born during embryonic amacrine cell genesis can convert to OFF bipolar fate in the absence of α-enhancer activity. This provides strong evidence for the competitive regulation model (C108), though the molecular mechanisms of transdifferentiation require further investigation.

results.result: Tgfb1i1−/− mice show reduced visual acuity despite normal photoreceptor and ON bipolar cell function. OptoMotry testing reveals significantly reduced visual acuity in P60 Tgfb1i1−/− mice compared to wild-type and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mice. However, ERG a-waves and b-waves are normal, indicating intact photoreceptor and ON bipolar cell function. Cell counts confirm normal numbers of these cell types, suggesting the visual deficits arise from alterations in amacrine cells and/or RGCs downstream of bipolar cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C109-C113 are supported by OptoMotry data (Figure 7A), ERG recordings (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and cell counts (Figure 7—figure supplement 2). The normal ERG responses with reduced visual acuity logically point to defects in inner retinal processing (C113), though the specific circuit alterations remain to be identified. The inference is reasonable but requires further investigation.

results.result: Tgfb1i1−/− and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas show opposite alterations in RGC light responses. MEA recordings reveal that Tgfb1i1−/− retinas have increased basal firing rate and mean spike number for light-ON responses, with sustained activity after light offset. Conversely, Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas show reduced basal firing, maximum spike rate, and mean spike number. The sustained responses in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas suggest P6α GABAergic amacrine cells disinhibit ON responses by acting on other inhibitory neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C114-C118 are supported by MEA recording data (Figure 7B-D). The opposite phenotypes in the two mutants are clearly documented with appropriate statistical analysis. The inference about disinhibition (C118) is supported by citations to previous studies on GABAergic amacrine cell function (Chávez et al., 2010; Demb and Singer, 2012; Eggers et al., 2013), though direct circuit mapping would strengthen this conclusion.

results.result: Tgfb1i1−/− and Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS mice show opposite visual detection and adaptation phenotypes. In visual detection tasks, Tgfb1i1−/− mice learn faster and show more sensitive light detection than wild-type. However, in visual adaptation tasks requiring detection after prior light exposure, Tgfb1i1−/− mice perform worse, suggesting slower re-sensitization. Conversely, Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas show faster re-sensitization despite lower light sensitivity.
results.evaluation: Claims C119-C124 are supported by behavioral test data (Figure 7E-G, Figure 7—figure supplement 3). The learning curves and performance metrics clearly demonstrate opposite phenotypes in the two mutants. The inference about re-sensitization rates (C122, C123) is reasonable based on the adaptation task performance, though the underlying mechanisms require further investigation.

results.result: P6α GABAergic amacrine cells control the tone of the light-ON retinal pathway, with proper cell numbers required for efficient visual adaptation. The light-ON pathway is augmented in Tgfb1i1−/− retinas (with extra P6α cells) making them hypersensitive but slow to re-sensitize, while it is attenuated in Pax6ΔPBS/ΔPBS retinas (with fewer P6α cells) making them hyposensitive but fast to re-sensitize. These cells likely inhibit other inhibitory neurons in the light-ON pathway, creating a disinhibitory circuit.
results.evaluation: Claims C125-C132 represent a synthesis of the MEA and behavioral data, supported by the collective evidence from Figure 7. The model of P6α amacrine cells controlling pathway tone (C125) is a reasonable inference from the opposite phenotypes. The prediction about inhibiting inhibitory neurons (C131) is logical given the GABAergic identity and sustained responses, though direct circuit mapping is needed. The conclusion about proper cell numbers (C132) is well-supported by the data.
